title: Annotatio IV §.XXIII: Psychic argument — natural body/blood → only natural participation; spiritual-only = not really
pass_a_gloss: Who, though they cannot deny that even most of all that which is Spiritually is in the thing itself, yet because the Supposit itself in the sacrament is a Material and Natural Thing (namely Christ’s body broken on the cross, and Christ’s blood poured on the cross), they contend therefore that there is no true participation of a Natural Thing except in some Natural mode; if therefore Christ’s body is participated by us only Spiritually, it is not participated Truly and in the thing itself.
pass_b_english: They concede that what is spiritual most of all is in the thing itself — yet the sacrament’s supposit is a material natural thing: Christ’s body broken and blood poured on the cross.
So they urge: a natural thing has no true participation except in some natural mode; if Christ’s body is received only spiritually, it is not received truly / in the thing itself.
source_text: Qui, licèt inficias ire nequeant, vel maximè re esse id, quod Spiritualiter est, Quia tamen Suppositum ipsum in sacramento, Res Materialis atque Naturalis est, (corpus putà Christi, in cruce fractum, & sanguis Christi, in cruce fusus;) contendunt ergò, Rei Naturalis nullam veram participationem esse, nisi Naturali aliquo modo; Spiritualiter igitur si solùm à nobis participetur corpus Christi, Verè, atque reipsà non participari.

lemmas.gloss: not participated Truly and in the thing itself

choices.english: not participated in the thing itself
choices.why: their denial of real spiritual participation

notes: Material natural supposit → natural-only participation claim.
